RISK=true because: (1) no full configured judge run or Oracle score exists for these bytes (raw-evidence-index scope says so), so 'oracle can score high' is plausible but unmeasured; the scripted driver does not walk every criterion (e.g. failed-send abort, job-open 0/51/2.5 refusals, activity filter completeness, candidate wording change were checked only by source); (2) P3 fragility in hro_unread_counts: when a message arrives in the open conversation, the refresh first shows unread 1 in the nav total badge (app.js:115-121) and catchUp->markRead clears only the row badge locally (threads.js:100-108); the total clears on the next SSE refresh (~0.3-1 s). A judge snapshot taken the instant the message appears could read total+1; the protocol's 'first snapshot at or after 15 seconds' makes this unlikely. Counter-probes: a conforming alternative that renders all activity would not be harmed; a broken app that only hides controls without server checks would fail the replay-based rows, and the golden enforces each rule server-side, so the golden is not passing by UI hiding.
